audit.whatIsWrong: The chart reads Skill, Sion, Sion, Skill, Skill, Sion, Sion. Every single whys[] row on the same page says the opposite — 'favours you', 'stays yours', 'is yours', 'favour you', 'clearly yours', 'stays yours', 'you hard-win'. The packet chart is Dr. Mundo on all seven rows.
audit.why: Three independent sources agree: the packet chart, all seven whys[], and a 54.78% Emerald+ win rate. Mechanically it holds up too — Decimating Smash is a visible charge Mundo simply walks out of, and Mundo's passive eats the one stun that would otherwise start a kill combo.
audit.corrected: Dr. Mundo on all seven stages, ratings raised to 6/10 early and 7/10 from level 3.

audit.whatIsWrong: diffRating and carryRating are empty strings.
audit.why: breakdown.difficulty and report[14].t on the same page both state 'difficulty 6/10, Sion carry threat 6/10', so the values exist and only the two fields are blank.

audit.whatIsWrong: The passive-versus-knockup interaction is absent, Decimating Smash's cooldown is given as 8s, and Roar of the Slayer's armour shred is never mentioned despite the page recommending Plated Steelcaps.
audit.why: Decimating Smash is 10/9/8/7/6 — 8s is rank 3, not rank 1 — and only a long enough charge knocks up and stuns. That stun and Unstoppable Onslaught's knockup are both Immobilizing effects, so Goes Where He Pleases resists the first one and drops a cannister that heals Mundo and shortens the passive. Roar of the Slayer (12/11/10/9/8, 800 range) reduces the armour of everything it passes through, which is a direct argument for health and magic resist over stacking plate.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t, phases[2].why and tradeGood now carry the real cooldown, the passive interaction and the armour-shred consequence.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[1] reads 'Stack Q slow to prevent him kiting your Poison Trail overlap'. Poison Trail is Singed's Q. Neither Dr. Mundo nor Sion has it.
audit.why: This is text copied from the Singed entry and left in place. A reader looking for their own ability will not find one.
audit.corrected: wants.you[1] now refers to Heart Zapper, which is what the Q slow actually holds him inside.

audit.whatIsWrong: Glory in Death is never mentioned, and tradeGood carries the PDF footer artifact '• • Dr. Mundo Top Lane Matchup Database 58'.
audit.why: Riot's text: after being killed Sion reanimates, and his attacks 'heal him, and deal bonus damage based on his target's maximum Health'. Against a Warmog's Mundo that is the one part of Sion's kit that scales with your own build, and it heals through the fight — which is exactly what Grievous Wounds answers. The supplied 'needs-antiheal' interaction is correct for this reason.
audit.corrected: spikes[3].text now names Glory in Death and the anti-heal requirement; tradeGood rewritten without the footer.

audit.whatIsWrong: One cooldown on the page and it was wrong.
audit.why: Decimating Smash 10s at rank 1, Soul Furnace 15s at rank 1 with a 3-second reactivate, Roar of the Slayer 12s at rank 1, Unstoppable Onslaught 140/100/60.
audit.corrected: The two that change your step-up now appear in breakdown.cooldowns.

edits.after: Level 1 is yours — Decimating Smash is a visible windup you walk out of, and it costs him 45 mana. Bonesaw from 975 and free-hit him every time he charges it.

edits.before: Line up your trajectory cleanly past enemy minion models. Launch an Infected Bonesaw (Q) to slow and chunk their current health, then step forward only when they are slowed to execute a quick auto-attack into an enhanced Blunt Force (E) reset. If they retaliate with heavy crowd control, your passive will pop a canister backward—walk over it immediately to heal up and walk away clean. • • Dr. Mundo Top Lane Matchup Database 58
edits.after: Decimating Smash is a charge you can see: step out of the cone while it winds up, then punish the recovery. Infected Bonesaw (Q) is 975 range on 4s and costs no mana, so you free-hit every wind-up. Your passive resists the first knockup and drops a cannister — walk over it, then auto into the E reset. Roar of the Slayer shreds armour, so answer him with health and magic resist, not plate.

edits.before: Sion's value shifts entirely to teamfight engage with ult and charged Q; in the side lane you hard-beat him 1v1, so you can freely split while he's forced to group.
edits.after: Sion's value shifts to teamfight engage; you hard-beat him 1v1 in the side lane. Kill him with Grievous Wounds up — Glory in Death heals him off your max health.

edits.before: Stack Q slow to prevent him kiting your Poison Trail overlap
edits.after: Keep the Q slow on him so he cannot walk out of Heart Zapper

notes:
REJECTED A SUPPLIED INTERACTION. missingInteractions offers: "Sion can cut your retreat with Unstoppable Onslaught (R) and you have no dash — hold Flash for the wall, not the damage." Unstoppable Onslaught creates no terrain. Riot's text is 'Sion charges in a direction... When he collides with an enemy he deals damage and knocks them up based on the distance he has charged.' The kit file's terrain flag is a tooltip-parsing misfire, and the instruction is to trust the description over the flag. Nothing about a wall was written.

Same call on the 'resistances-invalidated' interaction, half-accepted: Glory in Death genuinely deals bonus damage on the target's maximum health, so it is written in. Soul Furnace's percentHealth flag looks like it came from 'Sion... passively gains maximum Health' — that is Sion gaining health on kills, not percent-health damage — so I did not claim W punishes HP stacking.

The chart was inverted against all seven of its own whys[] rows and against the packet; flipped as one group.

wants.you[1] referenced Singed's Poison Trail — leftover text from another matchup.

PDF footer artifact '• • Dr. Mundo Top Lane Matchup Database 58' also sits in breakdown.trading and report[3].t; both are derived strings and want a scripted pass.
